the productivity of a multispecies cropping system may be higher, and that it is more resilient and stable than monoculture.
multispecies cropping systems are potentially more productive, more stable, more resilient, and more ecologically sustainable than monocultures.

the design, management, productivity, stability and resilience of multi-species cropping systems.
the productivity, stability, sustainability and resilience of traditional Indian cropping systems, and with the management of these systems.
the development of cropping systems that are more productive and stable, and that can be sustained in the long run.

multispecies systems are potentially more productive and stable, but they are harder to control and manage, and they are less resilient under intensification.

the productivity of traditional Indian cropping systems is not necessarily greater than that of modern ones, and that their ecological sustainability is not necessarily greater, but that they have the potential for greater stability and resilience.

the traditional multispecies cropping systems of India, if properly managed, have the potential to provide high levels of production, stability of yield, resilience to perturbations and ecological sustainability.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the productivity of a multispecies cropping system is greater than the average productivity of the component crops, and that its stability and resilience are also greater.

traditional Indian cropping systems, which are based on the imitation of natural systems, are potentially superior in production, stability, resilience, and ecological sustainability to modern monoculture systems, but they are harder to understand, and hence to manage, than modern systems.
traditional Indian cropping systems, with their high diversity, are potentially sustainable.

the traditional multispecies cropping systems of India are sustainable in the long term, and that the ecological principles underlying this sustainability can be applied in other situations to increase the sustainability of agriculture.
